{"successful": true, "data": {"results": [{"response": {"successful": true, "data": {"data": {"markdown": "[Skip to content](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/authenticate_#content) This page is available as Markdown at https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/authenticate\_.md. An index of every page is at https://developers.klaviyo.com/llms.txt. ## You will learn [\#](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/authenticate_\#you-will-learn) After reading this article, you will be able to distinguish which methods of authentication you should use for making calls with Klaviyo's server- and client-side APIs. You will also learn how to set custom scopes to protect you and your customers’ data. ## Server-side vs client-side APIs [\#](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/authenticate_\#server-side-vs-client-side-apis) A majority of Klaviyo’s APIs are server-side endpoints, which should be securely handled on your server rather than exposed in the browser. Handle sensitive information via server-side APIs, like bulk-creating events for one or more profiles. Client-side APIs are used to track and send user behavior data from the client to Klaviyo. They are designed to be called from publicly-searchable, client-side environments only (see [Client API reference](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/reference/create_client_subscription)). Klaviyo provides 3 methods of authentication including private key authentication and OAuth (used to call server-side APIs) and public key authentication (used to call client-side APIs). Read the table below to learn more about how each method can be used for authenticating API calls: | Server-side APIs | Client-side APIs | | --- | --- | | Private key authentication
All /api endpoints use API private keys to authenticate requests. If you do not use an API key for your requests, or if you use a key from the wrong account, your call will return an error. A 401 error indicates an invalid or missing API key. | OAuth
If you are a tech partner integrating with Klaviyo, we recommend using OAuth to [make authorized API calls](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/set_up_oauth). OAuth offers multiple benefits over a private key integration, including security, usability, improved rate limits, and the ability to be listed in Klaviyo's App Marketplace. | Public key authentication
All /client endpoints use a public API key: your 6-character company ID, also known as a site ID. We recommend using the [Klaviyo object](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/introduction_to_the_klaviyo_object) or our [Mobile SDKs](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/sdk_overview#mobile-sdks) for interacting with our client-side APIs. | ## Private key authentication [\#](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/authenticate_\#private-key-authentication) Private API keys can be used to read and write data to your Klaviyo account. Klaviyo allows you to generate multiple private keys for your applications. ### Create a private key [\#](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/authenticate_\#create-a-private-key) To create a private key: 1. Navigate to your account’s _Settings_ page and select **[API keys](https://www.klaviyo.com/settings/account/api-keys)**. 2. Under the _Private API Keys_ section, select **Create Private API Key**. ![Settings page with button to create a private API key.](https://files.readme.io/63e519eead1977ef41682d9be32ba3ddedf16c969cb6c2d7186c08b752aada8f-create_priv_key.png) 3. Provide a name for your private key and add any of the following scopes: - Custom Key Allows you to decide how much access to give the third party. - Read-Only Key Only allows third parties to view all data associated with the endpoint. - Full Access Key Allows third parties to create, delete, or make changes to anything associated with that endpoint. 4. When you have finished setting your key’s scopes, select **Create**. To protect your account from unauthorized access, you cannot view your private API keys in Klaviyo. After you have created your private API key, copy it to a secure location. ![Created private key with its Read/Write access endpoints.](https://files.readme.io/cfd0b2644992669c753febf25d64a01d61ad35b4bb50480219908cd112540807-private_key_created.png) Private keys will have the prefix pk\_ followed by a longer alphanumeric string. ### Use a private key [\#](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/authenticate_\#use-a-private-key) Private key authentication for `/api` endpoints is performed by setting the following request header: Copy ``` Authorization: Klaviyo-API-Key your-private-api-key ``` curlCopy ```curl curl --request GET \ --url https://a.klaviyo.com/api/{endpoint}/ \ --header 'Authorization: Klaviyo-API-Key your-private-api-key' \ --header 'accept: application/json' \ --header 'revision: 2026-10-15' ``` ## Public key authentication [\#](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/authenticate_\#public-key-authentication) Your 6-character public key, sometimes referred to as a site ID, is a short alphanumeric string that serves as the unique identifier for your Klaviyo account. Public keys cannot be used to access secure data in your account and are safe to share. Use your public key when you need to track people and events in client-side JavaScript code. Client-side API calls only require a public API key, also known as a `company_id`, for authentication: curlCopy ```curl curl --request POST \ --url 'https://a.klaviyo.com/client/subscriptions/?company_id=PUBLIC_API_KEY' \ --header 'content-type: application/json' \ --header 'revision: 2026-10-15' \ --data ' ... ``` ## OAuth [\#](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/authenticate_\#oauth) If you're building an app with Klaviyo, use [OAuth](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/set_up_oauth) to provide secure delegated access to users via access tokens (required to enter Klaviyo’s App Marketplace). When setting up OAuth, you must provide designated scopes for each API authorization request you'll want to make. ## Set custom scopes [\#](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/authenticate_\#set-custom-scopes) Setting custom scopes helps you protect your and your customers’ data by limiting what third parties can access. When requesting authorization to make API calls (OAuth), you should only request the scopes required to use your app. View the API reference documentation to understand which scopes you’ll need to define. For example, if your private key or Klaviyo app needs to create lists, your app needs the `lists:write` scope as shown in the following API reference documentation for the Create List endpoint: ![Create List API reference docs with lists:write scope highlighted](https://files.readme.io/1470bbc-v2_scopes_refdoc_submit_app.png) See the full list of scopes needed for each of our APIs below: **Available scopes for each API** | | | | --- | --- | | **API endpoint** | **Associated scopes** | | Accounts | `accounts:read` | | Campaigns | `campaigns:read`
`campaigns:write` | | Conversations | `conversations:read`
`conversations:write` | | Catalogs | `catalogs:read`
`catalogs:write` | | Coupons | `coupons:read`
`coupons:write` | | Coupon codes | `coupon-codes:read`
`coupon-codes:write` | | Data privacy | `data-privacy:read`
`data-privacy:write` | | Events | `events:read`
`events:write` (allows for creating/updating profiles) | | Flows | `flows:read`
`flows:write` | | Forms | `forms:read` | | Images | `images:read`
`images:write` | | Lists | `lists:read`
`lists:write` | | Metrics | `metrics:read`
`metrics:write` | | Profiles | `profiles:read`
`profiles:write` | | Push tokens | `push-tokens:read`
`push-tokens:write` | | Reporting | `campaigns:read`
`flows:read`
`forms:read`
`segments:read` | | Reviews | `reviews:read` | | Segments | `segments:read`
`segments:write` | | Subscriptions | `subscriptions:read`
`subscriptions:write` | | Tags | `tags:read`
`tags:write` | | Templates | `templates:read`
`templates:write` | | Tracking Settings | `tracking-settings:read`
`tracking-settings:write` | | Web Feeds | `web-feeds:read`
`web-feeds:write` | ## Additional resources [\#](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/authenticate_\#additional-resources) - [Make API calls with OAuth](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/set_up_oauth) - [Use Klaviyo's Postman collections](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/use_klaviyos_postman_collections) - [Introduction to the Klaviyo object](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/introduction_to_the_klaviyo_object) ![Project Logo](https://cdn.shopify.com/app-store/listing_images/8c8e0c8b87fd02ccf30e1a6de052e0ca/icon/CM384_2n0v8CEAE=.png) Ask AI By clicking “Accept all” or “Confirm”, you agree to the storing and use of cookies and online tracking technologies to enhance site navigation, personalise content, analyse your use of our sites, and assist with marketing and customer service efforts. This page is for Mailchimp Marketing API.

Every request to the Marketing API carries a credential. There are two kinds,
and which one you need depends on whose account data you’re reaching for.

## Choose a credential

An **[API key](https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/api-concepts/authentication/api-keys)** authenticates
against the account that created it. Use one when your code couples _your_
application’s data to _your own_ Mailchimp account. It requires no server to
handle a redirect, so it’s the fastest way to make a first request.

**[OAuth 2](https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/api-concepts/authentication/oauth-2)** authenticates
against an account belonging to someone else. Any integration a third party
installs needs it.

You can start development against your own account with a key and move to
OAuth 2 later; the request-signing mechanics below are identical for both.

**Note**: We strongly discourage asking your users to paste their API key into
your application. It gives you full control of their account, it can’t be
revoked for your application alone, and it makes you responsible for storing
someone else’s credential.

If you’re using one of the [official client libraries](https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/build/start-developing/client-libraries-and-sdks),
the library handles the signing details for you.

## Authenticate with an API key or OAuth 2 token

API keys and OAuth 2 access tokens are sent the same way. We’ll refer to both
as tokens.

You can use either HTTP Basic Authentication or Bearer Authentication.

HTTP Basic Authentication passes the token as the password, with any string as
the username:

```

```

Bearer Authentication passes it in the `Authorization` header:

```

```

## User access and revocation

Authentication is tied to the user who created the API key or authorized the
OAuth 2 app, not to the account. If that user is removed from the account, the
token is revoked.

Access is also bounded by the [user level (role)](https://mailchimp.com/help/manage-user-levels-in-your-account/)
of that user, and a role can change over time. An API action the role doesn’t
permit returns a [403](https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/api-concepts/errors#error-glossary). You can
check the role attached to a token with the [API Root endpoint](https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/api/root/list),
and compare what each role allows in
[this chart](https://mailchimp.com/help/manage-user-levels-in-your-account/#Compare_user_level_permissions).

When creating a key or authorizing an app, use an admin user where you can. If
you’re building an integration, consider telling the user when their role is
too limited for your application to work.

**Note**: You are responsible for the security of your tokens; store them in a
secure location on your server. Because of the risks of exposing a token,
Mailchimp does not support client-side calls to the Marketing API using CORS
requests.

This page is for Mailchimp Marketing API.

Every request to the Marketing API carries a credential. There are two kinds,
and which one you need depends on whose account data you’re reaching for.

## Choose a credential

An **[API key](https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/api-concepts/authentication/api-keys)** authenticates
against the account that created it. Use one when your code couples _your_
application’s data to _your own_ Mailchimp account. It requires no server to
handle a redirect, so it’s the fastest way to make a first request.

**[OAuth 2](https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/api-concepts/authentication/oauth-2)** authenticates
against an account belonging to someone else. Any integration a third party
installs needs it.

You can start development against your own account with a key and move to
OAuth 2 later; the request-signing mechanics below are identical for both.

**Note**: We strongly discourage asking your users to paste their API key into
your application. It gives you full control of their account, it can’t be
revoked for your application alone, and it makes you responsible for storing
someone else’s credential.

If you’re using one of the [official client libraries](https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/build/start-developing/client-libraries-and-sdks),
the library handles the signing details for you.

## Authenticate with an API key or OAuth 2 token

API keys and OAuth 2 access tokens are sent the same way. We’ll refer to both
as tokens.

You can use either HTTP Basic Authentication or Bearer Authentication.

HTTP Basic Authentication passes the token as the password, with any string as
the username:

```

```

Bearer Authentication passes it in the `Authorization` header:

```

```

## User access and revocation

Authentication is tied to the user who created the API key or authorized the
OAuth 2 app, not to the account. If that user is removed from the account, the
token is revoked.

Access is also bounded by the [user level (role)](https://mailchimp.com/help/manage-user-levels-in-your-account/)
of that user, and a role can change over time. An API action the role doesn’t
permit returns a [403](https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/api-concepts/errors#error-glossary). You can
check the role attached to a token with the [API Root endpoint](https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/api/root/list),
and compare what each role allows in
[this chart](https://mailchimp.com/help/manage-user-levels-in-your-account/#Compare_user_level_permissions).

When creating a key or authorizing an app, use an admin user where you can. If
you’re building an integration, consider telling the user when their role is
too limited for your application to work.

**Note**: You are responsible for the security of your tokens; store them in a
secure location on your server. Because of the risks of exposing a token,
Mailchimp does not support client-side calls to the Marketing API using CORS
requests.

Meet the Pinterest MCP

## The common language of AI and APIs

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables AI assistants to connect directly with external services. The Pinterest MCP Server brings Pinterest data into the AI tools you already use, giving agents native access to rich inspiration and creative signals — without custom code or fragile integrations. It helps teams move from idea to on-brand creative direction with Pinterest intelligence available right where they work.

Built for Pinterest workflows

Bring Pinterest Ads capabilities into the AI tools your team already uses. Query, analyze, and act through a consistent interface powered by the existing Pinterest API.

Open-standard integration

Built on MCP, with compatibility across tools such as Claude, Cursor, and VS Code.

Secure, scoped access

OAuth 2.0 authorization and granular permissions keep credentials protected and access appropriately controlled.

Less integration work

Skip custom API wrappers. The MCP server manages authentication, rate limits, and response formatting, so teams can move faster.

How it works

## Bring Pinterest intelligence into your AI workflow

Set up the Pinterest MCP Server once in your preferred AI environment. From there, you can search Pins, explore and manage Boards, uncover emerging trends, and access audience insights — all through natural-language prompts without leaving your chat or editor.

Find the performance stories hidden in your data.

Turn insights into action — create, update, and optimize with confidence.

Catch the next big idea before it takes off, using trends.

Turn audience and keyword signals into your next smart move.

```
 "type": "http",

}
```

# Authentication

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

Twilio SendGrid supports API keys delivered via Bearer token or Basic authentication, depending on the Twilio SendGrid functionality you are using. In addition to Bearer API key authentication, Twilio SendGrid recommends two-factor authentication (2FA) to improve security.

* * *

## API key

[api-key page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/for-developers/sending-email/authentication#api-key)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Authenticate to the Twilio SendGrid API by creating an API Key in the [Settings section of the Twilio SendGrid console(link takes you to an external page)](https://app.sendgrid.com/settings/api_keys "Settings section of the Twilio SendGrid console").

Twilio SendGrid requires using API keys because they are a secure way to talk to the Twilio SendGrid API that is separate from your username and password. If your API key gets compromised, you can delete and create a new API key and update your environment variables with the new key. API key permissions can be set to provide access to different functions of your account, without providing access to your account as a whole.

# HighLevel API Documentation

Modified on: Mon, 16 Nov, 2026 at 5:49 AM

HighLevel provides APIs that allow developers to build custom integrations, automate processes, and connect external applications with the HighLevel platform.

The APIs support contacts, conversations, calendars, workflows, payments, webhooks, and more.

API access is available across HighLevel subscription plans. However, certain endpoints and capabilities may require a higher-tier plan.

```
Important: API V1 reached end-of-support on December 31, 2025. Existing integrations may continue working, but API V1 no longer receives updates or technical support. Developers are encouraged to use supported API versions.
```

For complete endpoint references, visit the [Official HighLevel API Documentation](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/).

* * *

## **HighLevel API Documentation**

The official API documentation provides information about available endpoints, authentication, request parameters, response formats, and supported API versions. Developers can use this documentation to:

- Explore available API endpoints.

- Review authentication requirements.

- Check supported API versions.

- Build and maintain custom integrations.

- Understand endpoint-specific restrictions.


**Note:** New legacy API key generation is being phased out. Private Integration Tokens and OAuth 2.0 are the recommended authentication methods.

* * *

## **How to Use Versioned API Documentation**

Versioned API documentation allows developers to reference the correct API version when building or maintaining integrations.

1. Open the [HighLevel API Documentation](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/).

2. Select the required API version using the version switcher.



![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155085592327/original/ilcXF6VRPQX8XNizsUZPwtr8Dz7kLq6dYw.png?1794501570)

3. Review the available endpoints, parameters, and response formats.

4. Use the appropriate version when developing or updating integrations.


API V3 is available for supported endpoints. Availability varies by endpoint.

\[Screenshot: API documentation version switcher\]

* * *

## **API Access Across HighLevel Plans**

HighLevel offers API access across its subscription plans, including Starter, Unlimited, and Founder.

Both OAuth 2.0 and Private Integration Tokens (PIT) are available across plans. However, access to specific API endpoints depends on subscription eligibility, permissions, and scopes.

**API Availability by Plan**

| API Capability | Starter ($97/month) | Unlimited ($297/month) | Founder ($497/month) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OAuth 2.0 | Available | Available | Available |
| Private Integration Tokens | Available | Available | Available |
| Standard API Endpoints | Available\* | Available | Available |
| Higher-Tier Restricted Endpoints | Restricted | Restricted | Subject to endpoint eligibility |

\*Standard endpoint access is subject to applicable permissions and endpoint-specific restrictions.

For current subscription details, visit [HighLevel Pricing](https://www.gohighlevel.com/pricing).

**Plan-Restricted API Endpoints**

While standard API access is available across plans, certain operations require higher-tier subscriptions. The following endpoints are currently documented as requiring Founders plan access:

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Create Sub-Account | Create sub-accounts programmatically. |
| Enable SaaS for Sub-Account | Enable SaaS functionality for a sub-account. |

Refer to the [Official API Reference](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/) for endpoint-specific requirements.

* * *

## **API Authentication Methods**

HighLevel supports two primary authentication methods for modern API integrations.

**Private Integration Tokens (PIT)**

Private Integration Tokens allow developers to securely connect internal applications to HighLevel. They are suitable for account-specific integrations and allow permissions to be managed through assigned scopes.

**OAuth 2.0**

OAuth 2.0 allows applications to request authorized access to HighLevel accounts. It is commonly used for public integrations, Marketplace applications, and applications requiring user authorization.

**Note:** The availability of an authentication method does not guarantee access to every API endpoint.

For setup instructions, see [Private Integrations: Everything You Need to Know](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000003054-private-integrations-everything-you-need-to-know).

## **What Are the API Rate Limits?**

HighLevel applies rate limits to public API V2 requests using OAuth to maintain performance and stability.

| Limit Type | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Burst Limit | 100 requests per 10 seconds |
| Daily Limit | 200,000 requests per day |

These limits apply per Marketplace application and resource (Location or Company).

**Rate Limit Response Headers**

API responses include headers that help developers monitor usage:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit-Daily`

- `X-RateLimit-Daily-Remaining`

- `X-RateLimit-Interval-Milliseconds`

- `X-RateLimit-Max`

- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`


**Note:** These are the documented OAuth API V2 limits. Other APIs or Enterprise arrangements may have different limits.

* * *

## **How to Get Help or Support for HighLevel APIs**

HighLevel Support does not provide custom API development, code auditing, or integration setup services. However, developers can use the following resources:

- **API Bugs:** [Developer Support](https://developers.gohighlevel.com/support)

- **Developer Community:** [Join Developer Slack](https://developers.gohighlevel.com/join-dev-community)

- **Developer Resources:** [HighLevel Developers](https://developers.gohighlevel.com/)

- **Developer Events:** [HighLevel Events](https://www.gohighlevel.com/events)


### **How to Request a New API Endpoint**

If an endpoint is not available in the official API documentation, developers can submit a feature request through the [HighLevel API Documentation GitHub repository](https://github.com/GoHighLevel/highlevel-api-docs/issues).

Review the existing documentation before submitting a request.

* * *

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Is API access available on all HighLevel plans?**

Yes. HighLevel provides API access across Starter ($97/month), Unlimited ($297/month), and Founder ($497/month) plans. OAuth 2.0 and Private Integration Tokens (PIT) are available across all plans. However, access to specific API endpoints depends on subscription eligibility, required scopes, and permissions. The Founder Plan, formerly Agency Pro, includes higher-tier API capabilities and access to eligible restricted endpoints.

For current subscription details, refer to [HighLevel Pricing](https://www.gohighlevel.com/pricing).

**Q: Are OAuth 2.0 and Private Integration Tokens available on the Starter plan?**

Yes. Both authentication methods are available across plans. Access to specific endpoints depends on permissions, scopes, and plan eligibility.

**Q: What is the difference between Basic and Advanced API Access?**

These terms describe API capabilities associated with subscription tiers. The specific endpoints available depend on the plan and endpoint-level restrictions.

**Q: Does the Founder plan provide access to all API endpoints?**

Not necessarily. Endpoint availability depends on the applicable subscription entitlements, scopes, and API-specific requirements.

**Q: Is API V1 still supported?**

No. API V1 reached end-of-support on December 31, 2025. Existing integrations may continue functioning, but updates and technical support are no longer provided.

**Q: What authentication methods are supported?**

HighLevel supports Private Integration Tokens and OAuth 2.0 for modern API integrations.

**Q: Is API V3 available?**

Yes. API V3 is available for supported endpoints. Developers should review the API documentation for version-specific availability.

* * *

# Access your Gorgias REST API credentialsUpdated 5 months ago

The Gorgias REST API lets you read and write data in your helpdesk programmatically. To authenticate API requests, Gorgias uses HTTP Basic Authentication with three pieces of information: your base API URL, your email address, and an API key. You can find and manage all three from the REST API settings page in your helpdesk.

**Note:** API keys are tied to your individual account, not to the helpdesk as a whole.

For full API documentation, visit the [Gorgias Developer Documentation](https://developers.gorgias.com/).

* * *

### Requirements

- Available on all [Helpdesk plans](https://www.gorgias.com/pricing)
- The account owner and [admins](https://docs.gorgias.com/en-US/user-permissions-196938) can access the API credentials and create API keys

* * *

## Find your API credentials

You can find the **Base API URL** (`https://{your-domain}.gorgias.com/api/`), **Username** (the email address on your account), and **API key** in your Gorgias settings. If you don’t have an existing API key, you’ll have to create one first.

1. From your helpdesk, click the **Settings icon** in the bottom-left corner.
2. In the menu, locate **Account**, then select **REST API**.
3. Under **API Access & Credentials**, you'll find the **Base API URL**, your **Username**, and **Password (API Key)**.
4. Click **Copy** next to any field to copy it to your clipboard.

## Create an API key

If you haven't created an API key yet, the Password field will show a **Create API key** button instead of a key value.

1. From your helpdesk, click the **Settings icon** in the bottom-left corner.
2. In the menu, locate **Account**, then select **REST API**.
3. Under **Password (API Key)**, click **Create API Key**.

Your API key is generated immediately and displayed alongside the other credentials. Your API key grants full access to your account's data. Once you’ve copied it, store it somewhere secure and don’t share it with anyone.

### Reset your API key

You can reset your API key at any time. Resetting generates a new key and immediately invalidates the old one. Any integrations or scripts using the old key will stop working until they're updated with the new one.

1. From your helpdesk, click the **Settings icon** in the bottom-left corner.
2. In the menu, locate **Account**, then select **REST API**.
3. Next to the **Password (API Key)** field, click **Reset**.
4. Click **OK** to confirm.

## Import the Postman collection

The REST API settings page also includes a **Run in Postman** button. Clicking it imports the Gorgias Postman collection with your domain, email address, and API key pre-filled as environment variables, so you can start making requests immediately.

Next, click **Security and Access** in the menu on the left. Your API key is listed under the **Docs API** section.

![Security and Access](https://developer.helpscout.com/img/content/security-and-access.png)

**Note:** If you don't see an API key in your profile, that's because you haven't been granted the "Docs: Create new, edit settings & Collections" permission by the Account Owner or an Administrator.

## Authentication [Anchor link for: authentication](https://developer.helpscout.com/docs-api/\#authentication)

This is an HTTPS-only API. Authentication is based on API keys. Each API key is associated with a Help Scout user. Results returned from various responses are based upon the role of the user to which the API key is tied.

The API key is passed via HTTP Basic Authentication and goes in the username field. A dummy password, such as X, goes in the password field.

To try the API via curl on the command-line, the general form used would be:

```html
curl --user API_KEY:DUMMY_PASSWORD API_URL
```

```html

```

All API requests are made to **https://docsapi.helpscout.net/** and all requests are served over HTTPS. The current version is v1.

## Formats [Anchor link for: formats](https://developer.helpscout.com/docs-api/\#formats)

The API will only support JSON at this time.

## Correlation ID Response Header [Anchor link for: correlation id response header](https://developer.helpscout.com/docs-api/\#correlation-id-response-header)

All responses from the API contain a **Correlation-Id** header. This header contains a value (a UUID) which is used by Help Scout to trace interactions between our various APIs. In the case of an error and you're contacting the Help Scout team then include one or more of these IDs and developers will be able to assist quicker.

For instance if you wanted to print all headers on a curl request to access the Correlation-Id you would do the following:

```html
curl -v --user 60783dd23ef:X https://docsapi.helpscout.net/v1/collections
```

You would see console output like the following:

```html
 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
 Correlation-Id: 08d7aa72-4afb-4c2a-b027-45dacee1e1a0
```

## Rate Limiting [Anchor link for: rate limiting](https://developer.helpscout.com/docs-api/\#rate-limiting)

Each account is allowed to make a limited number of requests per 10 minute period. This limit is based on the number of Docs Sites the account has:

| Number of Sites | Rate Limit |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | 2000 requests every 10 mins |
| 2 | 3000 requests every 10 mins |
| 3 or more | 4000 requests every 10 mins |

Headers are returned with every API response to detail the current rate limiting status:

| Header Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| X-RateLimit-Limit | The maximum number of requests the account is permitted to make per 10 minute period |
| X-RateLimit-Remaining | The number of requests remaining in the current rate limit window |
| X-RateLimit-Reset | The number of seconds until the current rate limit window expires |

Response code 429 is returned when the limit has been reached.

**Note:** Usage of the Help Scout Docs administration interface generates requests to Docs API. These requests also count towards the rate limit.

## Response Envelopes [Anchor link for: response envelopes](https://developer.helpscout.com/docs-api/\#response-envelopes)

The API returns one of three envelopes depending upon the request issued:

1. Single Item Envelope
2. Collections Envelope
3. Error Envelope

### Single Item Envelope [Anchor link for: single item envelope](https://developer.helpscout.com/docs-api/\#single-item-envelope)

All dates/times are returned in ISO8601 format and in UTC timezone.

```xml

{

 "id": 1234,
 ...
 "createdAt": "2012-07-17T13:41:01Z"
 }
}
```

### Collections Envelope [Anchor link for: collections envelope](https://developer.helpscout.com/docs-api/\#collections-envelope)

```xml
 },\
 {\
 "id": 5678,\
 ...\
 "createdAt": "2012-07-15T08:12:15Z"\
 },\
 ...\
 ]
}
```

### Error Envelope [Anchor link for: error envelope](https://developer.helpscout.com/docs-api/\#error-envelope)

```xml
Status: 404 Not Found
{
 "code": 404,
 "error": "Resource not found"
}
```

# Authentication

Copy

To access the Intercom API, you have two authentication options depending on whether you app is public or private.

- An [Access Token](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication#access-tokens) is for if you're using the API to access data in **your own** Intercom workspace, in other words, building a private app.
- [OAuth](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication#oauth) is for if you're building a public app that accesses **other people's** Intercom data.

## Access Tokens

Access Tokens can be used for the following cases:

- You want to use the API to build a private Intercom app
- You want to run scripts to create or get data from your Intercom workspace
- You want to use the API to programmatically automate certain actions in your Intercom workspace

In all of these cases, the data you are accessing is your own team's customer data.

![A image showing the use of a personal access token to work with data on the Intercom API](https://developers.intercom.com/assets/pat-flow.a57707b73af31a3ae69f2b18a4c0ce9d8341d659a8649917e833232025570ed9.71a4f21c.png)

### How to get your Access Token

We provide you with an Access Token as soon as you [create an app](https://www.intercom.com/signup/developer) on your workspace.

You can find your Access Token in the **Configure > Authentication** section in your app within the [Developer Hub](https://app.intercom.io/a/apps/_/developer-hub/app-packages).

![Access Token](https://developers.intercom.com/assets/e77cdff-access_token.4c1ae57393655175c1f2455f5ec4052968f3788fdef7cbccd1e74cae1baa7b9f.71a4f21c.png)

It is also visible on the **Test & Publish > Your Workspaces** page. This displays workspaces that have the app installed. More about how this works can be found in the [Installing & Uninstalling Apps guide](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication/installing-uninstalling-apps).

Access Tokens are issued to a teammate

An Access Token is issued to the teammate who installed the app on the workspace, or who last regenerated the token. Its access to conversations is limited by that teammate's conversation access, in addition to the app's scopes. See [Conversation access is limited by the installing teammate](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication/oauth-scopes#conversation-access-is-limited-by-the-installing-teammate).

Never give your Access Token to a third-party

Your Access Token can give access to your private Intercom data and should be treated like a password. If an app provider asks you for your Access Token, please do not provide it. Instead, let us know - apps are required to use OAuth rather than asking users for Access Tokens.

## OAuth

You should use OAuth if:

- You are requesting access to other people's Intercom accounts/data (for example, through an integration you've built)
- You currently ask people for their API Keys to request resources on their behalf
- You want to make it easier for your customers to share their customers' data with you

![OAuth Flow](https://developers.intercom.com/assets/x8kdkklsq424lxuz7sh1_oauth_cropped.72b26d1b307b50411b414a8f33759513922c6d65806be67a4eb92a896617e841.71a4f21c.png)

### Getting Started with OAuth

To set up and test the OAuth installation flow in your development workspace by [following this tutorial](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication/setting-up-oauth).

Never ask users for their Access Token

Asking your users for their Access Tokens rather than implementing OAuth is against our terms of service and may result in your API access being revoked.

## How to use the token

Once you have a token, whether an access token or a token via the OAuth process, simply provide it as an `Authorization:Bearer` header in your requests, as shown below. If you want to go deeper on how the `Authorization:Bearer` header works please check out the [full spec here](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750).

```
$ curl \
-s https://api.intercom.io/users/5321a20f72cdbb4192000013 \
-H 'Authorization:Bearer <access_token>' \
-H 'Accept:application/json'
```

Alternatively, helper functions are provided in some of our SDKs to authorize via Access Tokens. This means you don't need to specify the header explicitly - it's all done under the hood.

```
intercom = Intercom::Client.new(token: '<access_token>');
```

```
{"token": '<access_token>'}
```

```
var client = new Intercom.Client({ token: '<access_token>' });
```

# Bold BI

Bold BI integrates with LiveAgent to create real-time dashboards from data, offering insights into company performance. Suitable for businesses of all sizes, the integration is customizable and enhances workflow by displaying incoming inquiries efficiently.

[External Integration](https://www.boldbi.com/resources/integrations/liveagent/)

- **Partner website** [Learn More](https://www.boldbi.com/?utm_medium=referral&utm_source=liveagent&utm_campaign=integration)

- **Partner Privacy Policy** [Bold BI Privacy Policy](https://www.boldbi.com/legal/privacy/)


## Bold BI integration

**Bold BI** helps to gather data that can be turned into unique dashboards with real-time information. The integration with LiveAgent enables you to create customizable dashboards displaying incoming inquiries and company performance metrics efficiently.

## What is Bold BI?

Bold BI is a platform that helps you gather data in a [dashboard](https://www.liveagent.com/customer-support-glossary/ "Discover LiveAgent's comprehensive glossary of customer service and help desk terms. Perfect for beginners and pros to boost knowledge!"), which you can share. As a result, it can provide actionable insights into your company’s performance.

## How can you use it?

Use data from LiveAgent to create a dashboard with real-time information about your incoming inquiries. LiveAgent provides you with a lot of data daily. With Bold BI you can benefit from that data by migrating the information to view it in a simple, readable dashboard.

![LiveAgent Logo](https://images.liveagent.com/images/logo-inline-banner.svg)

## How to integrate Bold BI with LiveAgent

Please follow the guide below to start using Bold BI with LiveAgent. Before you get started, you’ll need to be logged in to your Bold BI account and have your LiveAgent API key ready. If you need help finding your API key in LiveAgent, please refer to the \[LiveAgent API documentation\]( [https://support.liveagent.com/840770-Complete-API-reference](https://support.liveagent.com/840770-Complete-API-reference) ‘Explore LiveAgent’s Complete API Reference for detailed documentation on agents, conversations, customers, and more.’).

### Step 1: Add a new data connection

In Bold BI, click the **Data Source** button in the configuration panel to add a new data connection.

![Bold BI Data Source button](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/databutton.png.webp)

### Step 2: Create a new connection

Click on **CREATE NEW** to launch a new connection from the connection type panel.

![Bold BI Create New connection](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/datasourcebutton1.png)

### Step 3: Select LiveAgent connection

In connection type panel, select **LiveAgent** connection button.

![Bold BI LiveAgent connection button](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/liveagent_button.png)

### Step 4: Configure data source

The **NEW DATA SOURCE** configuration window opens.

![Bold BI NEW DATA SOURCE configuration window](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/liveagent_panel.png)

### Step 5: Enter API URL

Enter an API in the URL text box which must be a valid **REST API**. Refer to the LiveAgent API documentation.

![Bold BI API URL configuration](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/url_liveagent.png)

### Step 6: Choose REST API method

Choose a method for the REST API.

![Bold BI REST API method selection](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/method_liveagent.png)

### Step 7: Add header information

If required, add header information by clicking **ADD**.

![Bold BI header information](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/header_liveagent.png)

### Step 8: Configure refresh settings

Choose **Refresh Settings** for the REST API.

![Bold BI Refresh Settings](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/refresh_webdataconnection.png)

### Step 9: Select data format

Choose either **JSON** or **CSV** as a **Data Format** for the REST API.

![Bold BI Data Format selection](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/data_webdataconnection.png)

### Step 10: Choose authentication type

Choose an authentication type for the REST API.

![Bold BI authentication type](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/authentication_webdataconnection.png)

### Step 11: Preview and connect

Click **Preview & Connect** button in the **NEW DATA SOURCE** configuration panel.

![Bold BI Preview and Connect button](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/liveagent_connectiontype.png)

### Step 12: Choose schema

A new window opens – **Choose Schema(s)**. Select a schema and click connect.

![Bold BI Choose Schema window](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/asknicelyschemawindow.png.webp)

### Step 13: Design data view

Go to the data design view window with selected table schema. Drag and drop the table.

![Bold BI data design view](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/dataview_asknicely.png.webp)

### Step 14: Save data source

Click **Save** button to save the data source with valid name.

![Bold BI Save data source](https://images.liveagent.com/images/processed/integrations/save_asknicely.png.webp)

## Benefits of Bold BI integration

- **Real-time dashboards**: Create customizable dashboards with live data from LiveAgent
- **Data visualization**: Transform complex data into simple, readable visualizations
- **Performance insights**: Gain actionable insights into your company’s performance
- **Workflow enhancement**: Display incoming inquiries efficiently for better team coordination
- **Scalability**: Suitable for businesses of all sizes

## Frequently asked questions

What is Bold BI?

Bold BI is a powerful business intelligence dashboard software that helps you visualize your data and gain actionable insights. It allows you to create and share interactive dashboards.

How does the LiveAgent integration with Bold BI work?

The integration allows you to connect LiveAgent as a data source in Bold BI. You can then create real-time dashboards using your LiveAgent data, such as ticket statistics and agent performance metrics.

{"successful": true, "data": {"results": [{"response": {"successful": true, "data": {"data": {"markdown": "For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs.

 [Skip to content](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication#gitbook-main-content)

The Pylon API uses [Bearer](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6750#section-2.1) authentication. This means you’ll need to pass your API token in the header of your request:

Copy

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

Generate an API token in the [Pylon dashboard](https://app.usepylon.com/settings/api-tokens).

### API regions[Direct link to heading](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication\#api-regions)

Pylon’s API is available in two regions. Use the base URL that matches where your Pylon tenant is hosted:

- US region: https://api.usepylon.com

- EU region: https://api.eu.usepylon.com


Both regions use the same API endpoints and authentication. Configure your integration to use the region where your Pylon tenant is hosted.

You can tell a token's region from its prefix:

Prefix

Region

`pylon_api_eu_`

EU

`pylon_api_`

US

Tokens created before prefixes were introduced have no prefix. Sending a token to the other region's API returns `401` with the `wrong_region_token` error code, and the message names the correct URL.

Once you've created a token, call the [`/me`](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference/me) endpoint to retrieve details about your organization and confirm your token works.

## Create an API token[Direct link to heading](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication\#create-an-api-token)

Only Admins can create and manage API tokens.

1. Go to **Settings > Integrations & dev > API**. On the **Tokens** tab, click **Create API Token**.

2. Enter a **Name**.

3. Choose who the token acts as:



 - Leave **Act as user or bot (optional)** empty to give the token its own identity. Pick a **Role** to control what it can access, and optionally upload an icon.

 - Or select a teammate or bot. The token uses that user's current role and permissions.


4. Optionally, add an **IP allowlist** (see below).

5. Click **Create** and copy the token. Pylon shows it only once.


Tokens don't expire, and their access is controlled only by the role. There are no separate scopes.

### Roles[Direct link to heading](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication\#roles)

A token with its own identity uses the role you pick when you create it. You can change the role later with **Edit**. Older tokens that have no role act as Admin.

A token that acts as a user or bot has no role of its own. It always uses that user's current role, so changing the user's role changes what the token can do.

See [Roles and user management](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/platform/roles-and-user-management) for what each role allows.

### Who actions are attributed to[Direct link to heading](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication\#who-actions-are-attributed-to)

- **Token with its own identity:** actions show up under the token's name and icon.

- **Token that acts as a user or bot:** actions are attributed to that user or bot.


### Bots[Direct link to heading](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication\#bots)

Bots are identities for automation, so API activity is attributed to the bot instead of to a teammate. Bots can't sign in to Pylon.

To create one, go to **Settings > Workspace > Users**, open the **Bots** tab, and click **New Bot**. Give it a name, an avatar, and a role. Then select the bot under **Act as user or bot** when you create a token.

### IP allowlist[Direct link to heading](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication\#ip-allowlist)

Add IP addresses (for example `203.0.113.10`) or CIDR blocks (for example `203.0.113.0/24`) to restrict where the token can be used. You can add up to 20 entries. If the list is empty, the token works from any IP.

Pylon checks the public IP address your requests come from, so add the public egress IPs or ranges of the servers that call the API. Private addresses such as `10.0.0.0/8` or `192.168.0.0/16` never match.

A request from an address that isn't on the list returns `401` with the `invalid_api_token` error code.

## Manage tokens[Direct link to heading](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication\#manage-tokens)

The **Tokens** tab shows each token's **Acts as**, **Token preview**, **Role**, **Created by**, **Last used**, and **Created** values. From the **…** menu on a token you can:

- **Edit:** change the name, role, or IP allowlist.

- **Duplicate Token:** create a new token with the same settings.

- **Rotate:** generate a new token value. The current token stops working immediately.

- **Delete:** permanently revoke the token. Calls using it stop working immediately.

- **View Activity:** open the token's request logs.


## Review API request logs[Direct link to heading](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication\#review-api-request-logs)

Only Admins can view request logs. Go to **Settings > Integrations & dev > API** and open the **Logs** tab, or choose **View Activity** from a token's **…** menu to see only that token's requests.

Filter by token, or choose **All tokens**, and by a date range of up to 90 days. The range defaults to the last 7 days. Each request shows when it was made, the token, who it acted as, the method, endpoint, response status, source IP, user agent, and request ID. Requests made with a token that was since deleted still appear.

Requests rejected for authentication or rate limits aren't logged, and older requests may not show a token.

### When tokens are revoked automatically[Direct link to heading](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication\#when-tokens-are-revoked-automatically)

When a user is deactivated, Pylon deletes:

- every API token that user created, and

- every API token that acts as that user.


Before you deactivate someone who created tokens your integrations rely on, create replacement tokens from another Admin's account.

An Admin who has created Admin-role tokens can't be moved to a different role until those tokens are deleted.

Pylon’s API can be used to programmatically access and take action on data within Pylon.

Only Admin users can create API tokens. To learn more about Admins, see [Roles & User Management](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/platform/roles-and-user-management).

Some common use cases for our API include:

- Fetching information about customers

- Fetching information about issues

- Creating issues programmatically


Check out our [API Reference](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference) for specifications on all endpoints. To call the API from TypeScript, Python, or Go, use our [SDKs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/sdks), with pinned installation commands and upgrade guidance for each language.

Prefer the terminal? Try our experimental [Pylon CLI](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/cli). It’s an early release and may change.

Before you build an integration, read:

- [Authentication](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication) for creating tokens, roles, and regions

- [API conventions](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/conventions) for IDs, timestamps, pagination, search filters, update behavior, files, and slugs

- [Rate limits](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/rate-limits) for request limits and how to handle `429` responses

# Verifying an end user's email address

[![image avatar](https://support.zendesk.com/system/photos/4423414114074/profile_photo.jpeg)](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/profiles/1263082071689)

[Anton de Young](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/profiles/1263082071689)

Edited Jul 16, 2026

When you have an activated help center, verification emails are sent to users who register. Ideally, users will verify their email address as soon as they receive the verification email message, but agents can also verify an end user's email address on the user's behalf.

[What's my plan?](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/5411234991258-plan)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **All Suites** | Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus |

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Support** | Team, Professional, or Enterprise |

Summary: ◀▼

You can verify end users' email addresses on their behalf to ensure they can submit support requests and access the help center. Verification is essential when registration is required, preventing unverified users' tickets from appearing in active views. Agents and admins can verify emails, resend verification emails, and identify unverified addresses to manage user access and support ticket flow effectively.

When you have an activated help center, verification emails are sent to users who register.
Ideally, users will verify their email address as soon as they receive the
verification email message, but agents can also verify an end user's email
address on the user's behalf.

If you require users to [register before submitting a\\
request](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408893912986#topic_iv2_zmj_2z), but a user doesn't verify their email address, they
won't be able to create a password to sign in to your help center to submit
a request. Any support requests submitted by the unverified user through
email will remain in limbo in the Suspended tickets view. The ticket won't
appear in your other views, and an agent cannot work on it.

This article covers the following topics:

- [Verifying a user's email address on their behalf](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408886752410-Verifying-an-end-user-s-email-address#topic_ryz_p4g_b2b)
- [When to verify for\\
users](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408886752410-Verifying-an-end-user-s-email-address#topic_fcq_ggg_b2b)
- [Identifying unverified email addresses](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408886752410-Verifying-an-end-user-s-email-address#topic_fy2_tsh_15b)

## Verifying a user's email address on their behalf

Agents and admins can verify a user's email address on their behalf.
Agents can verify end-user accounts only. Admins can verify all
users except the account owner.

You can also [resend\\
the verification email](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408832398618) so that the user can
verify their own email address. Or you can verify user email
addresses when adding users via the API (see [Zendesk API: Users](https://developer.zendesk.com/api-reference/ticketing/users/users/)).
In that case, you might want to disable verification emails for
users (see [How can I disable end user verification\\
emails?](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408885856538)).

Note: The options for verifying email addresses are not available
until you [activate your help\\
center](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408846795674#topic_ckn_wc4_qy).

**To verify a user's email address on their behalf**

1. After you add the user (see [Adding end\\
 users](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408893585178)), open the [user's profile](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408822762650).
2. Click the down arrow next to the user's email address
 and select **Verify Now**.
![](https://zen-marketing-documentation.s3.amazonaws.com/docs/en/email_verify_now.png)


The user's email address is immediately verified. If the user has
submitted any support requests, those requests are _not_
automatically added as tickets to views but can be manually
recovered from suspended tickets.

After the user's email address has been verified, you may also want your
users to have a password. The password is required if users want to
sign in to your help center. Like email verification, the user
should create their own password. However, you can create passwords
for them. You must be an administrator to use either of these
options:

- Reset the password in the Security tab of the user's
profile (see [Resetting user passwords](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408831970202).)
- Use the Zendesk API (see [Zendesk API:\\
Users](https://developer.zendesk.com/api-reference/ticketing/users/users/))

## When to verify for users

If your Zendesk Support is configured to require users to register, each
user must create an account, verify their email address, and also
create a password. You may want to verify for your users in these
cases:

- **Testing** \- You are testing your workflow, and you
want to create test users and tickets to test
automations and triggers. You can add some test
users for email accounts that you own and easily
verify those new users.
- **Adding Agents or Known Users** \- When adding new
agents (or other known users) to your account
because you know that their email addresses are
legitimate, you can verify them as you add
them.

## Identifying unverified email addresses

If a user doesn't have a verified primary email address, a warning icon
(![](https://zen-marketing-documentation.s3.amazonaws.com/docs/en/suspended_icon.png)) is
displayed next to the email address on the **Customers** page. If
you hover over the icon, you’ll see the text “Unverified email.”

![Suite all](https://zen-marketing-documentation.s3.amazonaws.com/docs/en/announcement_tag_2.png)

If an email address is unverified and owned by an existing user with a
verified primary address, Zendesk flags the ticket with **User has**
**yet to confirm ownership of the address used to deliver this**
**email**. If you aren't certain the email was sent from
that user, consider [resending a verification\\
email](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408832398618), reassigning the ticket to a security group for
review, or solving the ticket with due caution.

![](https://zen-marketing-documentation.s3.amazonaws.com/docs/en/email_unverified_user_flag.png)

On the Customers page, you can search for users with verified
or unverified identities using the `is_verified`
term. However, users with any verified identity, not just an email
address, are included in the search results. For example:

- **is\_verified:false Sunita** returns all
users named Sunita who don't have a verified
identity

- **is\_verified:true** returns all users with
a verified identity

### [oauth access token permalink](https://developer.zendesk.com/api-reference/introduction/security-and-auth/\#oauth-access-token) OAuth access token

The Zendesk API supports OAuth authorization flows. For more information, see [Using OAuth authentication with your application](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408845965210).

An OAuth token gives access to a single Zendesk instance (the one with the [OAuth client](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408845965210#topic_s21_lfs_qk) used to create the token).

OAuth access tokens also permit client-side API requests. See [Making cross-origin, browser-side API requests](https://developer.zendesk.com/documentation/ticketing/using-the-zendesk-api/making-cross-origin-browser-side-api-requests/) in the Zendesk API guide.

In your requests, specify the access token in an Authorization header as follows:

```
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
```

Example:

```
Authorization: Bearer gErypPlm4dOVgGRvA1ZzMH5MQ3nLo8bo
```

If you use curl to test different endpoints, you can use the following format:

```
curl https://obscura.zendesk.com/api/v2/users.json \ -H "Authorization: Bearer gErypPlm4dOVgGRvA1ZzMH5MQ3nLo8bo"
```

Access tokens can be up to 184 characters long.

### [global oauth access token permalink](https://developer.zendesk.com/api-reference/introduction/security-and-auth/\#global-oauth-access-token) Global OAuth access token

If you plan on making an app, integration, or bot available to multiple Zendesk customers, you must use global OAuth access tokens to authenticate Zendesk API requests. You may not use regular API tokens or OAuth tokens because the [Zendesk Developer Terms](https://www.zendesk.com/company/agreements-and-terms/zendesk-developer-terms/) prohibits Zendesk customers from sharing their API credentials with you. The requirement to use global OAuth tokens doesn't apply if you're developing applications or integrations for internal use.

API tokens are different from OAuth tokens, which are detailed in the previous section. API tokens are auto-generated passwords in the Zendesk Admin Center.

**Warning:** As passwords, API tokens can be used to impersonate anyone in the account, including admins. Make sure to keep them secure. Delete any unused tokens. Delete a token at once if you suspect it's been compromised and create another one if necessary. For a more secure alternative, use OAuth access tokens as described above.

API tokens are managed in the Admin Center interface at **Apps and integrations** \> **APIs** \> **Zendesk API**. The page lets you view, add, or delete tokens. More than one token can be active at the same time. Deleting a token deactivates it permanently.

You can have up to 256 tokens. If you're at the limit, you must delete an existing token to add a new one. Accounts that currently have more than 256 tokens have a limit of 2048 tokens.

Basic authentication is used for API tokens. The credentials must be sent with the request in an Authorization header.

Use the following format for the credentials:

```

jdoe@example.com/token:6wiIBWbGkBMo1mRDMuVwkw1EPsNkeUj95PIz2akv
```

```
Authorization: Basic amRvZUBleGFtcGxlLmNvbS90b2tlbjo2d2lJQldiR2tCTW8xbVJETXVWd2t3MUVQc05rZVVqOTVQSXoyYWt2
```

```
curl https://obscura.zendesk.com/api/v2/users.json \ -u jdoe@example.com/token:6wiIBWbGkBMo1mRDMuVwkw1EPsNkeUj95PIz2akv
```

The Zendesk v2 API is an SSL-only API, regardless of how your account is configured.

All connections to the Zendesk API must support the TLS 1.2 protocol. Support for TLS 1.0 and 1.1 was removed in June 2018.

Connections to the API must also support the SNI extension to TLS.

If you connect to Zendesk through a client library, make sure it supports both TLS 1.2 and SNI.
